purpose: Frozen requirements specification for UETGPT's market-wide RAG storage architecture screen, established BEFORE vendor research began. Every requirement is classified per the mandate's own taxonomy so it is clear which facts can eliminate a candidate outright versus which only inform scoring after hard-gate survivors are known. Not modified after seeing candidate results.

fixed_project_facts.raw_dense_payload_bytes: ~63MB (20,652 vectors x 768 dims x 4 bytes float32)
fixed_project_facts.retrieval: dense + lexical, application-level RRF, reranker, citation hydration
fixed_project_facts.traffic: very low, with realistic long idle periods (university holidays/semester breaks)
fixed_project_facts.budget: $0 recurring infrastructure cost unless the user explicitly changes it
fixed_project_facts.self_hosted_infrastructure_assumption: No reliable always-on host exists beyond the developer's Windows/WSL machine, per direct user confirmation. Self-hosted candidates (Family C) are therefore treated as conceptual-only in this screen, not researched to the same depth as managed candidates.

knowledge_store_interface_reference.note: CRUD and concurrency requirements below are written directly against this real interface, not a generic paraphrase.

requirements.statement: A genuinely permanent $0 tier for the current workload - not trial credits, not a time-boxed trial, not one-time node-hours.
requirements.rejection_rule: If the only zero-cost availability is temporary trial credits or a time-boxed trial, reject unless another genuinely permanent free tier exists.

requirements.statement: Comfortably supports 20,652 x 768-dim vectors plus ANN/index overhead, metadata, chunk IDs, filter indexes, canonical text if stored there, lexical index, temporary rebuild overhead, and old generations during replacement - not just raw vector bytes.
requirements.growth_tolerance: should preferably tolerate ~2-3x current corpus without redesign

requirements.statement: No auto-deletion after inactivity; no suspension requiring multi-minute or manual/dashboard/API resume before serving a real user request. The single gate that eliminated the most candidates in this screen.
requirements.not_automatically_disqualifying: Transparent, fully automatic scale-to-zero that resumes within seconds on the next request.
requirements.likely_disqualifying: Explicit manual resume, or any resume latency beyond a few seconds, or any policy leading to permanent data deletion after a realistic idle window.
requirements.prohibited_workaround: Synthetic/artificial keep-warm traffic to evade a provider's inactivity policy is not permitted.

requirements.statement: Exceeding the free quota must fail closed (hard block/throttle, no card required, no surprise charges) or offer a hard spending cap. Automatic uncapped paid overage is a serious risk for a strict-$0 architecture.

Supports >=768 dense dimensions, the current vector count, a usable distance metric (must verify what the existing system actually uses rather than assume cosine), stable custom IDs, and metadata filtering. Do not change UETGPT's embedding model merely to fit a provider's free tier.
Must be capable of implementing all ten KnowledgeStore methods (insert/upsert/update/delete/bulk-ingest/replay-idempotency/document-replacement/stale-chunk-deletion) without permanent accumulation.

Not literally 'must expose compare-and-swap.' The actual invariant: a stale ingestion generation must never become the authoritative retrieval result after a newer generation has committed. Native CAS/transactions satisfy this outright; otherwise a generation-scoped-ID + authoritative-generation-filtering protocol must be credible. If no credible mechanism exists at all, that is a FAIL.

Must work from a Convex action: Node.js runtime, fetch/HTTPS-based, no raw TCP, no assumed persistent connection pool. A provider that only works from a normal VM but cannot cleanly operate from this execution environment is not viable.
Credentials must be able to remain server-side. Reject designs requiring privileged database credentials in a browser bundle, public environment variables, or client JavaScript.
Prefer one store over three services/scheduler/keep-alive/custom-sync-daemon/special-proxy for similar capability. Architecture complexity is an operational cost even at $0 invoice cost.

Prefer designs where chunk IDs, embeddings, RRF, reranker, and the evaluation dataset remain under UETGPT's control. Avoid unnecessary dependency on proprietary ranking semantics when existing application logic already works.

If an external provider's lexical subsystem is immature or expensive, retaining Convex lexical retrieval may be the better design. Quantify Convex's minimal storage, lexical-index storage, and rebuild IO before dismissing this architecture.

For any finalist: can vectors be exported, can canonical text remain outside, is the data model portable, is there an open-source/self-host equivalent. Do not select a free tier that creates an expensive future trap without documenting it.
Recall@10 >= 0.98 against exact-cosine ground truth, using the same methodology already established for Turso (scripts/turso-ann-benchmark.mjs). Not executed in this screening phase.
p50/p95/p99 latency with full context (sample count, index size, topK, metadata in/out, region, network env). Not executed in this screening phase.

HitRate@K, MRR, nDCG via scripts/stage_e_retrieval_eval.py in backend-export mode against the real corpus exported via convex/crawl/exportCorpus.ts, compared to a frozen Convex baseline. Not executed in this screening phase.

Full 7-scenario lifecycle matrix (fresh load, exact replay, changed document, removed chunk, removed document, interrupted ingestion+retry, concurrent generations) plus a concurrent-generation torture test. Not executed in this screening phase.

Per-feature classification: GA/Stable/Public Preview/Beta/Alpha/Private Preview/Deprecated. A production recommendation should preferably not depend on a Public Preview/Alpha retrieval primitive; if it must, classify the candidate CONDITIONAL, not an unconditional winner.

Community/practitioner findings (GitHub issues, forums, case studies) labeled ANECDOTAL or PRODUCTION_CASE_STUDY, never used as proof of current quotas or lifecycle behavior - only official current documentation is authoritative for those facts.
Community popularity, vendor marketing claims ('fastest', 'enterprise-grade'), and vendor benchmark rankings are not decision factors.
